key_insight: GraphBEAT outperformed tested graph and sequence models for gastrointestinal cancer risk prediction while using substantially less computation.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support earlier risk stratification for pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancers using longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory results.
method: Groups clinical events into time buckets and builds patient-specific, temporally directed graphs.
Encodes event identity, observed value, and timing in graph nodes.
Combines context-aware, time-decay message passing with multi-head attention pooling.
evidence_signal: In multi-site EHR evaluations at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times, GraphBEAT outperformed GraphSAGE, GAT, GCN, Transformer, and LSTM baselines, with over 250× fewer FLOPs per patient and over 20× fewer parameters than the sequence baselines.
watch_item: The abstract does not report cohort size, absolute predictive performance, or prospective validation, limiting assessment of clinical readiness.
paper_title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
